findings.claim: The ordinary code-finding row negates the verdict test, so a finding below the broken-record boundary cannot enter the open repair path.
findings.intended: Select review/open and plan DISPATCH reviewer, WRITE reviewLog, then NEXT, as specified by fixtures/scenarios.json:3.
findings.actual: The open predicate is false because finding !== finding is false; broken-record is also false at ordinal 1, and no other row matches, so evaluation fails with no row.

findings.claim: The review table has no unconditional default row, so an unclassified verdict does not terminate with the intended review-unclassified block.
findings.intended: Select BLOCK:review-unclassified and terminate BLOCK, as specified by fixtures/scenarios.json:9.
findings.actual: Every conditional row is false and there is no default, so table evaluation fails with no matching row instead of producing the block.

findings.claim: The persisted review log declares no reader, so the evidence written for cross-session review progression has no declared consumer.
findings.intended: A later review-flow consumer reads the persisted review evidence so progression can be reconstructed after session loss, as required by body.md:5 and references/purpose.md:3.
findings.actual: reviewLog has readers: [], leaving the written artifact with no declared reader.

notes: Blinded review only. The permitted lint command reported L5 at TABLES.review.rows and L10 at ARTIFACTS.reviewLog.readers.
